tasks.title: The expressions feature, options, error surface and extension parsing
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Add the off-by-default feature `expressions` to `dxn_dtcg` with optional dependencies `rquickjs` (package `quickjs-jit`, `=0.14.1`, `default-features = false`, features `std` and `loader`) and `oxc = "=0.153.0"` (features for parser, semantic, transformer and codegen with source maps), declared once in `[workspace.dependencies]` (d-feature-options). Add the always-present surface: `EXPRESSION_EXTENSION`, `ResolvedToken::snapshot` (always `None` until t02), `DtcgError::Expression { resource, path, message }`, `DtcgDiagnosticCode::Expression`. Add the feature-gated `dxn_dtcg::expressions` module with `ExpressionOptions` (defaults and `with_*` setters for step budget, memory limit, stack limit and precision; module registries come later) and `RuntimeOptions::with_expressions`, keeping `RuntimeOptions` `Clone`/`Debug`/`Eq`. Parse and validate the token expression object per EXP-2 (only with expressions enabled), with an internal parsed form t02 consumes.

New groups: `tests/expressions_disabled.rs` (EXP-1; must compile and pass with and without the feature, so feature-dependent parts sit behind `#[cfg(feature = "expressions")]`) and `tests/expressions_format.rs` (EXP-2; `#![cfg(feature = "expressions")]`). PLT-1 is proven by `check-default-graph`.

tasks.title: Evaluate expressions inside token resolution
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Implement the QuickJS session (d-engine-sessions: lazy creation per resolving call, generated wrapper module per token, inputs through `JSON.parse`, value conversion with the integral rule, non-JSON rejection, depth bound and rounding) and wire it into `Resolver::token_cost` per d-dual-resolution: resolve `$value` as today, resolve inputs with `resolve_value` at `Position::Unchecked`, evaluate, convert, charge `max_value_nodes`, check depth, validate against the effective type, set `snapshot`, and record the token's cost from the result. Map caught exceptions to `DtcgError::Expression` (positions refined in t04). The sandbox hardening and limits are t03; keep a single place where the context is created so t03 extends it.

New group `tests/expressions_evaluation.rs` covering EVAL-1..3: snapshot and type rules, inputs through aliases, pointers and nested literals, hop/node/depth limits on inputs, missing targets, cycles through inputs, aliases to expression tokens, result conversions and rejections, rounding defaults and `None`, literal strings.

tasks.title: Sandbox, limits and determinism
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Harden the context per d-engine-sessions, adapting nsh's `sandbox.rs` (intrinsic subset, deleted `eval`, throwing function constructors, frozen prototypes with accessor members, frozen `globalThis`, throwing `Math.random`, frozen inputs, no dynamic `import()`), and enforce the step budget (interrupt ticks per evaluation, uncatchable), the memory limit and the stack limit, mapping them to `LimitExceeded { kind: "expression steps" | "expression memory" }` and `DtcgError::Expression`. Keep the runtime usable after every failure.

New group `tests/expressions_sandbox.rs` covering SBX-1..3, including repeated resolution equality, evaluation-order independence, no leakage between expressions or calls, and a document without expression tokens resolving under a memory limit too small to create an engine.

tasks.title: TypeScript expressions and authored error positions
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Strip `ts` expressions with oxc per d-typescript (follow nsh's `compile_native` without JSX), and map syntax and runtime error positions back to the authored expression text for `js` and `ts` (wrapper offsets; for `ts`, through the source map). Map `DtcgError::Expression` to `DtcgDiagnosticCode::Expression` in `DtcgDiagnostic::from_error`.

New group `tests/expressions_typescript.rs` covering EVAL-4: type annotations, `as`, `satisfies`, generics and interfaces erased; syntax and runtime errors with line and column in `js` and `ts`, including multi-line expressions; the diagnostic code.

Confirm `to_document` round trips with expressions on and off.

New group `tests/expressions_apis.rs` covering EVAL-5: each API with an expression token, affected resolution after editing an input target, an expression object and an unrelated token (affected set and `apply_affected` equal to a full resolution), and the export round trip.

sprints.title: Final-review repairs: stack top, module state, diagnostic names, docs

tasks.title: Align QuickJS's stack top with each evaluation
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Final-review finding E-F3: rquickjs updates QuickJS's stack top only with its `parallel` feature, so the stack limit was measured from where the session was created while the guard measured from each evaluation. Call `JS_UpdateStackTop` at session setup and with `Guard::begin` at the start of every evaluation (expression module, expression call, module component). The guard noticed an overflow only when QuickJS allocated past the threshold while throwing, which depends on what it allocated before (one more module flipped the result), so a stack overflow could still be caught: compiled code now passes every value a `catch` or `finally` receives to the internal `check` (insertions only, no line breaks, positions mapped back), which trips the guard on QuickJS's stack overflow `RangeError`; one that reaches the engine uncaught trips it too. New group `tests/expressions_stack_top.rs` (alias chains with and without an earlier expression token, evaluations nested in input resolution, engine recursion through nested arrays, every `catch`/`finally` form, module top-level code, positions around `try`), plus a wasm32 case in `expressions_wasm.rs`.

tasks.title: Freeze module values after their top-level code
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Final-review finding E-F1: tokens share a module within a resolution, so a module's exported or internal objects could carry state from one token to another. Every JavaScript/TypeScript module ends with generated code that deep-freezes its namespace and top-level bindings (objects, arrays, functions, classes and prototypes) through the internal module `dxn.dtcg/freeze`; generated local names avoid the module's own. The cycle tests in `expressions_modules.rs` observe ES order through a counter instead of a shared array. New group `tests/expressions_module_state.rs`, plus a wasm32 case. The docs state what freezing cannot reach (reassigned module-level `let`s, closure variables, `Map`/`Set`/typed-array contents) and that module functions must be pure.

tasks.title: Keep only standard error names in diagnostics
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Final-review finding E-F2: expression code sets an error's name, so the redacted diagnostic keeps only the standard JavaScript error names and reports `Error` for any other `...Error` name. New group `tests/expressions_diagnostic_names.rs`.

tasks.title: Shared module state as the owner decided
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Per the owner's decision on final-review finding E-F1 (option A, 2026-10-25): SBX-4 and EVAL-6 supersede SBX-3 and EVAL-5 with the exception for module state that module functions change. Keep modules evaluated once per resolution (MOD-5) and their top-level values deep-frozen (t18); chapter 15 and the website `expressions` page state, in their sandbox/limits and determinism sections, that such state is shared within one resolution, that module functions must be pure, and that results depending on it are guaranteed neither independent of evaluation order nor equal between `apply_affected` and a full resolution. Evidence: `expressions_module_state` (frozen values, affected equals full), `expressions_stack_top` (order independence of stack limits), `expressions_sandbox` (determinism, no engine without expression tokens) and `expressions_apis` (every API, affected resolution). Widened by the owner's decision on review finding S6-F2 (option A): the exception covers module state any code changes, token expressions included, including the contents of `Map`s, `Set`s, typed arrays, `ArrayBuffer`s and `DataView`s a module holds; modules may hold and export such collections.

sprints.title: Second final-review repairs: async overflows, shared compilation, color, docs

tasks.title: Keep stack overflows uncatchable through async code and wrapped errors
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Second final-review finding E2-F1 and sprint review findings S7-F1..F7: stack overflows escaped through async functions, parameter defaults, iterators closed by a throw and wrapped errors. QuickJS-jit serves small objects from 4 KiB arenas, so the error it throws at its limit reaches the guard's allocator only sometimes; detection therefore does not rely on it. An async function's rejection goes through QuickJS's host promise rejection tracker, which trips on a stack overflow (unwrapped like `check`); the body of every plain `return` method or arrow (what closing an iterator calls, discarding what it throws) runs through `checked`, an arrow wrapper that keeps `this`, `arguments` and scoping; the catch/finally check stays; `note_overflow` unwraps `SuppressedError`/`AggregateError`. The regular expression compiler reports its overflow only after unwinding, so patterns built at run time (`RegExp`, string patterns of `match`/`matchAll`/`search`) nest at most 20 groups and classes like literals (a class nests in another only with the `v` flag, in both the wrapper and the literal bound), `RegExp(re)` returns `re`, and `RegExp.prototype.compile` is removed. The guard's threshold lies a quarter of the limit (at most 64 KiB) below QuickJS's limit. HARDEN removes `Array.fromAsync` and `AsyncDisposableStack`. New group `tests/expressions_async_overflow.rs`; `expressions_stack_top` pins the deterministic pattern error. Parameters the wrapped `return` body redeclares with `var` or a function are passed through the arrow, so they keep sharing their binding (S7-F8).

tasks.title: Name shared expression modules from their text
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Second final-review finding E2-F2: tokens with the same expression text share one compiled module, which was named after the first token to compile it, so stack traces and `apply_affected` depended on evaluation order. The module is named from a SHA-256 digest of its text. New group `tests/expressions_shared_compilation.rs`.

tasks.title: Clip HSL/HWB and contrast into sRGB, keep near-gray hues, reject non-finite native arguments

New groups `tests/color_gamut_contrast.rs` and `tests/expressions_native_finite.rs`; `expressions_builtin` expects the bridge's message for `dtcg.s(NaN)`.

tasks.title: Stack overflows as the owner decided

Chapter 15 and the website `expressions` page name the exception in their stack bullets. Evidence: `expressions_sandbox`, `expressions_stack_top` and `expressions_async_overflow`.

sprints.title: Third final-review repair: wrapped overflows however deep

tasks.title: Unwrap wrapped stack overflows however deep
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Third final-review finding E3-F1: `check` gave up after 10,000 wrapped values and the Rust `is_stack_overflow` after 1,000, so a long `DisposableStack` chain hid an overflow. The internal module's `isOverflow` now walks wrapped `SuppressedError`s and `AggregateError`s until none are left, visiting each object once (a `WeakSet`) and reading only data properties; `check`, the promise rejection tracker and `note_overflow` all use it, so the walk runs under the step budget. Tests in `tests/expressions_async_overflow.rs` with chains of 100, 2,000 and 12,000 callbacks, overflow first and last, caught synchronously and in an async body (they fail with a cap of 1,000).
